title: 4. Citizenship at the Commencement of the Constitution (Article 5)

blocks.content: At the commencement of this Constitution, every person who has his domicile in the territory of India and who was born in the territory of India shall be a citizen of India.

rows: Person was born in the territory of India
Either of whose parents was born in the territory of India
Ordinarily resident for at least 5 years immediately preceding 26 Jan 1950

items: Domicile in India is an essential pre-requisite under Article 5; without domicile, citizenship under this article cannot be claimed.
Article 5 applies exclusively to citizenship status as on January 26, 1950, not for post-commencement acquisition.
Questions frequently test the specific timeline for ordinary residence under Article 5(c), which is 'not less than 5 years immediately preceding commencement'.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 5 determines citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution on January 26, 1950.
Having a domicile in the territory of India is the fundamental pre-condition for citizenship under this Article.
In addition to domicile, a person must fulfill at least one of three conditions: born in India, either parent born in India, or resident for 5 years.
The minimum period of ordinary residence required prior to commencement under Clause (c) is five years.
